title: Common Errors
markdown:
## From the assembler (NASM)

| Message | Usual cause |
|---|---|
| `invalid combination of opcode and operands` | the operands do not fit the instruction: different sizes (`mov eax, rbx`), two memory operands, a constant as the destination, or `div 10` (the divisor must be a register or memory) |
| `operation size not specified` | neither operand is a register, so write the size: `mov qword [rdi], 0` |
| `symbol 'x' not defined` | a misspelt label, a local `.label` used from another function, or a routine name typed wrong |
| `label 'x' inconsistently redefined` / `symbol 'x' redefined` | the same label twice; use local labels (`.done`) inside functions |
| `expression syntax error`, or `label, instruction or prefix expected at start of line` | often a label or function named after a NASM keyword (see below) |
| `impossible combination of address sizes` | mixing 32- and 64-bit registers in one address: `[rdi + ecx*4]` |
| `invalid effective address` | a scale other than 1, 2, 4 or 8, or `rsp` as the index |
| `parser: instruction expected` | a typo in an instruction, or a label without its colon |

## Names NASM keeps for itself

Some words cannot be used as labels or function names, because NASM reads them as keywords. Ones that catch people out: **`abs`**, **`absolute`**, **`times`**, **`byte`**, **`word`**, **`dword`**, **`qword`**, **`rel`**, **`seg`**, **`wrt`**, **`section`**, **`global`**, **`extern`**, **`align`**, **`struc`**, and the register names. Choose another name: `abs_value`, `multiply`, `text`.

## From the linker (ld)

| Message | Means |
|---|---|
| `cannot find entry symbol _start` | no `_start` label, or it is not `global` (the website adds `global _start` for you) |
| `undefined reference to 'x'` | called but never defined, such as a misspelt routine |
| `relocation truncated to fit` | a 32-bit address form used for a label that is too far away: use `[rel label]` and `lea` |

## When it runs

| What you see | Usual cause |
|---|---|
| **Segmentation fault** (exit code 139) | reading or writing an address that is not yours: a register used as a pointer that holds a number, a missing `[rel ...]`, a store into `.text` or `.rodata`, or running off the end of the program because the exit system call is missing |
| **Floating point exception** (exit code 136) | `div` or `idiv` by zero, or a quotient too big because `rdx` was not cleared (`xor edx, edx`) or sign-filled (`cqo`) first |
| a crash right after `ret` | the stack was not left as it was: a `push` without its `pop`, or `rsp` changed and not restored |
| a test says "changed rbx" (or rbp, r12 to r15) | the function used a callee-saved register without saving it with `push` and restoring it with `pop` |
| a value disappears after `call print_int` | it was in a scratch register (`rax`, `rcx`, `rdx`, `rsi`, `rdi`, `r8` to `r11`); keep it in `rbx` or `r12` to `r15` |
| a loop never ends | the counter is changed by a call inside the loop, or the jump goes to the wrong label |
| a comparison seems backwards | a signed jump (`jl`, `jg`) used for unsigned values, or the other way round; or the flags were changed between the `cmp` and the jump |
| garbage in the upper half of a result | an 8- or 16-bit write (`mov al, ...`) left the rest of the register as it was: clear it first or use `movzx` |
